subject: science
passage: In large stretches of the open ocean, the water holds plenty of nitrate and phosphate yet supports surprisingly little phytoplankton, a puzzle that oceanographers in the late 1980s traced to a scarcity of iron. Experiments since the 1990s have confirmed the diagnosis: when ships have spread dissolved iron across patches of such water, phytoplankton have bloomed within days. <u>From this result, some have drawn a proposal: fertilize the oceans with iron on a vast scale, and the resulting blooms will draw carbon dioxide out of the atmosphere.</u> The step from bloom to lasting carbon storage, however, is longer than the proposal implies. Carbon is kept out of the atmosphere for centuries only if the plankton sink into the deep ocean before being consumed, and in most experiments only a small fraction appears to have done so.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It presents a proposal drawn from an experimental result, which the text then says overlooks a necessary condition.
choices.B: It states the hypothesis that the iron experiments described in the previous sentence were designed to test.
choices.C: It explains why waters rich in nitrate and phosphate nonetheless support little phytoplankton.
choices.D: It provides evidence that adding iron to the ocean would remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere for centuries.

explanation.why: The underlined sentence turns the experimental finding (iron causes blooms) into a proposal to fight climate change. The next sentence says the step to "lasting carbon storage" is "longer than the proposal implies": the plankton must sink to the deep ocean, and in most experiments few did. So the text presents the proposal and then identifies the condition it overlooks.
explanation.A: Correct. The proposal assumes blooms will remove carbon, but the text explains that lasting removal also requires the plankton to sink, which rarely happened.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The experiments tested whether iron scarcity limits phytoplankton; the proposal was drawn from their results afterward.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The first sentence explains the puzzle by pointing to iron scarcity; the underlined sentence describes a proposal.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The underlined sentence states a proposal, not evidence, and the text goes on to doubt that the carbon would stay out of the atmosphere.
